items.title: 股價較高點回跌逾4成！SpaceX首份財報將掀牌 AI、星鏈、星艦受檢驗
items.title_en: Stock Falls Over 40% From Recent Highs! SpaceX's First Earnings Report to Spotlight AI, Starlink, Starship Scrutiny
paras: SpaceX(SPCX-US)將於美東時間周二(4日)盤後公布2026會計年度第2季財報，市場預料結果可能引發股價劇烈波動，目前以人工智慧(AI)業務營收、虧損與資本支出這三大數字最受關注。
這家由全球首富馬斯克領軍的公司，目前市值約1.4兆美元，數周前一度高達3兆美元，目前股價仍為2026年預估營收的35倍，使本次財報成為市場焦點。
Cantor Fitzgerald分析師Colin Canfield表示，目前市場預估值分歧極大，「幾乎沒有人真正知道會開出什麼數字」，財報結果可能與市場預期出現相當大的落差。
AI財務數字與展望
SpaceX目前將業務劃分為三大部門，包括：太空(火箭發射與星艦計畫)，連網(星鏈衛星網路)，AI(主要為今年2月併入的xAI業務)。
三者當中，以AI業務最受市場關注，其在2026年第1季營收為8.18億美元，但營業虧損高達25億美元，單季資本支出更達77億美元。
市場將聚焦三項關鍵指標：AI營收是否快速成長，虧損是否收斂，
AI資本支出是否持續擴大。
SpaceX已與Anthropic及Google(GOOGL-US)簽署AI資料中心租賃協議。兩者當中，Google合約尚未開始貢獻營收，Anthropic每月約12.5億美元的租賃合約，則於5、6月逐步放量，但實際認列營收及獲利率仍不明朗。
投資人也將關注SpaceX對今年下半年及2027年AI業務展望，以及利用星鑑部署低成本AI運算衛星的測試時程。
星艦進度、星鏈用戶
星鑑(Starship)於7月完成第13次飛行測試，市場將關注：第14次測試何時進行，以及星鑑的研發支出規模。
SpaceX在第1季的太空事業新增廠房與設備支出約11億美元。
太空部門2025年營收41億美元，營業虧損為6.57億美元。而獵鷹九號(Falcon 9)在第2季的火箭發射約36次，多數為星鏈(Starlink)任務，因此不會認列為太空部門收入，市場預料投資人仍將把焦點放在AI及星鏈，而非火箭發射業務。
星鏈方面，截至第1季季末的全球訂戶已達1030萬戶，較一年前約500萬戶倍增。該項業務在2025年的營收為114億美元，營業利益44億美元。
市場將關注星鏈的訂戶成長速度、每位用戶平均收入(ARPU)，以及
企業及政府客戶訂單。Canfield預期，SpaceX將首度揭露更多有關星鏈的營運指標。
Canfield預期，這份財報將優於市場預期，且全年獲利展望可望上修。
目前華爾街平均預估第2季營收將為69億美元，而稅息折舊及攤銷前利益(EBITDA)為21億美元
全年部分，營收估為390億美元，EBITDA為173億美元。不過市場預估分歧極大。
解禁賣壓仍是股價隱憂
SapceX周一盤中一度跌至每股104.83美元、創上市新低，但終場反彈5.68%，收在每股114.53美元。然而周一收盤價仍比6月16日首次公開發行(IPO)後創下的歷史收盤高點(201.80美元)回跌了43%。
其中一項憂慮來自IPO禁售期即將屆滿。根據規劃，8月6日將有約9.12億股解禁，約一周後另有3.19億股解禁。
市場擔心早期投資人可能趁機獲利了結，對股價形成賣壓。但也有分析認為，市場通常會提前反映已知消息，因此真正解禁後未必再出現新一波拋售。
paras_en: SpaceX (SPCX-US) will release its fiscal 2026 Q2 earnings after market close on Tuesday (the 4th) Eastern Time. The market expects the results could trigger sharp stock volatility, with AI revenue, losses, and capital expenditures being the three most watched figures.

Led by the world’s richest man Elon Musk, the company now has a market value of about $1.4 trillion, after briefly reaching $3 trillion a few weeks ago. Its share price still trades at roughly 35 times the projected 2026 revenue, making this earnings release a focal point for investors.

Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Colin Canfield said market valuation estimates are wildly divergent, "almost nobody really knows what numbers will be reported," and the earnings could differ substantially from expectations.
AI Financial Numbers and Outlook

SpaceX currently groups its operations into three divisions: Space (rocket launches and the Starship program), Connectivity (the Starlink satellite network), and AI (mainly the xAI business that was folded in February this year).

Among them, the AI segment draws the most market attention. It posted Q1 2026 revenue of $818 million but an operating loss of $2.5 billion, and capital expenditures for the quarter reached $7.7 billion.
The market will focus on three key AI metrics: whether AI revenue is growing quickly, whether losses are narrowing, and whether AI capex continues to expand.

SpaceX has signed AI data‑center leasing agreements with Anthropic and Google (GOOGL-US). Google’s contract has not yet contributed revenue, while Anthropic’s lease is about $1.25 billion per month and is expected to ramp up in May and June, though actual recognized revenue and profit margins remain unclear.
Investors will also watch SpaceX’s outlook for AI in the second half of this year and in 2027, as well as the schedule for testing low‑cost AI‑computing satellites deployed via Starship.
Starship Progress and Starlink Users
Starship completed its 13th flight test in July. The market will watch when the 14th test will occur and the scale of R&D spending for Starship.
SpaceX’s Space division recorded roughly $1.1 billion in new plant and equipment spending in Q1.

The Space segment generated $4.1 billion in revenue for 2025 and an operating loss of $657 million. Falcon 9 performed about 36 launches in Q2, most of which were Starlink missions and therefore not counted as Space‑division revenue. Investors are expected to keep their focus on AI and Starlink rather than on launch activity.

For Starlink, global subscriber numbers reached 10.3 million by the end of Q1, roughly double the 5 million a year earlier. The business posted $11.4 billion in revenue and $4.4 billion in operating profit in 2025.

The market will monitor Starlink’s subscriber growth rate, average revenue per user (ARPU), and enterprise and government contracts. Canfield expects SpaceX to disclose more operational metrics for Starlink for the first time.
Canfield anticipates the earnings will beat market expectations and that the full‑year profit outlook could be revised upward.

Wall Street currently forecasts Q2 revenue of $6.9 billion and EBITDA of $2.1 billion. For the full year, revenue is projected at $39 billion with EBITDA of $17.3 billion, though estimates vary widely among analysts.
Unlocking‑related Selling Pressure Remains a Stock Risk

SpaceX’s shares fell intraday on Monday to $104.83, a new low since the company went public, but recovered 5.68% to close at $114.53. Even so, Monday’s close was still 43% below the post‑IPO historical high of $201.80 set on June 16.
One concern stems from the upcoming end of the IPO lock‑up period. About 912 million shares are slated to unlock on August 6, with another 319 million shares scheduled to unlock roughly a week later.

The market worries early investors may seize the chance to cash out, creating selling pressure on the stock. Some analysts, however, argue that markets usually price in known events ahead of time, so a post‑unlock wave of selling may not materialize.

items.title: DRAM供給吃緊延續到2027年！輝達評估下調Rubin Ultra HBM規格
items.title_en: DRAM Supply Tightness Extends to 2027! Nvidia Evaluates Down‑Scaling Rubin Ultra HBM Specs
paras: 根據 TrendForce(集邦科技) 最新記憶體產業研究指出，受 DRAM 供不應求格局將延續至 2027 年、且原廠 HBM4e 驗證進度存在變數影響，自今年第三季起，輝達對次世代 Rubin Ultra 的 HBM 配置已從原先基準設計「HBM4e 12hi」，改為並行評估 HBM4e 8hi、HBM4 12hi、HBM4 8hi 等方案，目前尚未定案。
《財聞社》報導，這家市場研究與顧問諮詢機構表示，今年上半年以來，存儲器供給緊缺已數度迫使 AI 晶片下修 DRAM 規格，雲端服務供應商 (CSP) 與 Server OEM 陸續下調 RDIMM 容量；輝達也因為 LPDDR5X 短缺恐持續至 2027 年，決定將 Vera Rubin Superchip 模組的 SOCAMM 容量減半。
Rubin Ultra 在 2025 年至 2026 上半年之間均以 HBM4e 12hi 為基準，第三季上旬起才開放評估較低規格，主因在於兩大瓶頸：一是 2027 年整體 DRAM 供應維持緊缺，原廠可分配給 HBM 的晶圓產能受限；二是 HBM4e 12hi 的驗證與量產良率提升進程仍不確定。

根據分析，輝達在 Rubin Ultra 世代主要目標是拉高 I/O 速度，次要目標才是 GPU 出貨規模成長；若最終調降規格，傾向從堆疊層數 (Stack Layers) 著手，這意味著單顆 GPU 的 HBM 搭載容量與可出貨顆數之間，將出現新權衡。HBM4e 能否如期完成驗證，決定 I/O 速度能否從 Rubin 的 8–11.7Gbps 躍升至 14–16Gbps，否則僅能靠 HBM4 優化至 11–12Gbps。
集邦預估，2027 年 HBM 出貨單位年增約 50–60%，仍追不上需求端成長，而在供不應求下，議價權偏供應商，HBM 單價大漲成產業共識。
面對供給量縮與採購成本雙壓，不止輝達，部分 CSP 也正考慮調降下一代自研 ASIC 的 HBM 容量設計。
paras_en: According to TrendForce's latest memory‑industry research, the DRAM shortage will persist through 2027, and uncertainties in the OEMs' HBM4e validation schedule add further risk. Starting in Q3 of this year, Nvidia has shifted the HBM configuration for the next‑generation Rubin Ultra from the original baseline design of "HBM4e 12‑hi" to a parallel evaluation of several options, including HBM4e 8‑hi, HBM4 12‑hi and HBM4 8‑hi, with no final decision yet.

The report from "Finance News Society" notes that the market‑research and consulting firm says the tight memory supply since the first half of this year has repeatedly forced AI chip makers to downgrade DRAM specifications, and cloud‑service providers (CSPs) and server OEMs have gradually reduced RDIMM capacities. Nvidia, facing a shortage of LPDDR5X that could last until 2027, has also decided to halve the SOCAMM capacity of its Vera Rubin Superchip module.

Rubin Ultra was slated to use HBM4e 12‑hi as the baseline for both 2025 and the first half of 2026, with lower‑spec options only opened for evaluation in early Q3. The move is driven by two major bottlenecks: first, overall DRAM supply remains tight through 2027, limiting the wafer capacity that OEMs can allocate to HBM; second, the validation and yield‑improvement timeline for HBM4e 12‑hi remains uncertain.

Analysts say Nvidia's primary goal for the Rubin Ultra generation is to boost I/O speed, with GPU shipment volume being a secondary objective. If the specs are ultimately lowered, the likely approach is to reduce the stack layers, which creates a new trade‑off between the HBM capacity per GPU and the number of GPUs that can be shipped. Whether HBM4e can complete validation on schedule will determine if I/O speeds can jump from Rubin's current 8–11.7 Gbps to 14–16 Gbps; otherwise, only modest gains to 11–12 Gbps via HBM4 optimization are possible.

TrendForce estimates that HBM shipments will grow about 50–60% year‑over‑year by 2027, still lagging behind demand growth. In a supply‑constrained market, bargaining power shifts to suppliers, and a sharp rise in HBM unit prices has become industry consensus.
Facing both reduced supply and higher procurement costs, Nvidia is not alone; some CSPs are also considering lowering the HBM capacity designs for their next‑generation in‑house ASICs.

items.title: AI投資邏輯變了？雲端巨頭變「收租王」 基礎設施鏈卻遭無情血洗
items.title_en: Has AI Investment Logic Changed? Cloud Giants Turn Into "Rent Collectors" While Infrastructure Chains Face Brutal Valuation Cuts
paras: AI 投資熱潮正在迎來新的分水嶺。近期美股科技股財報季出現明顯分化，微軟 (MSFT-US) 、亞馬遜 (AMZN-US) 等雲端服務供應商（CSP）股價大漲，市值創下新高；另一方面，SK 海力士 (000660KS) 、鎧俠等 AI 基礎設施供應鏈企業卻遭遇重挫，部分記憶體股價甚至腰斬。市場正在重新評估 AI 浪潮的受益者，焦點也從過去「誰投入最多資本」轉向「誰能將投資轉化為現金流」。
過去兩年，市場追捧的是 AI 基礎建設擴張邏輯，只要雲端巨頭提高資本支出（CapEx），GPU、HBM、光通訊、交換器、PCB、電源與資料中心等相關供應鏈便同步受惠。但如今投資人開始提出更嚴格的問題：巨額 AI 支出最終流向誰的收入，又會沉澱成誰的折舊成本？
市場正在形成新的共識，AI 資金並未消失，而是開始從「賣鏟子的人」流向「利用鏟子創造商業模式的人」。
雲端巨頭證明 AI 需求正在轉化為收入
本輪市場重新定價的重要訊號，來自雲端服務商展現出更強的 AI 變現能力。微軟 Azure 第二季營收年增 43%，亞馬遜 AWS 年增 37%，創下 18 季以來最快增速，Google Cloud 則年增 82%，三大雲端業者合計雲端業務年化收入達 3890 億美元。
更重要的是，AI 需求不再只是來自少數前沿模型公司。微軟披露，商業剩餘履約義務（RPO）達 6780 億美元，年增 84%，新增需求主要來自銀行、製造、醫療與政府等傳統企業客戶，顯示 AI 應用正逐步滲透企業核心流程。
亞馬遜 AWS 也透露，企業客戶正簽署多年期承諾合約，需求仍高於供給。市場認為，長約模式代表 AI 算力需求已從測試階段走向正式商業部署，雲端業者因此開始具備更穩定的收入能見度。
基礎設施鏈遭遇估值重新定價
與雲端巨頭形成對比的是 AI 基礎設施供應鏈的劇烈修正。SK 海力士雖繳出歷來最強財報，營業利益大增 557%，但股價仍大幅下跌；市場關注的已不只是企業是否成長，而是成長速度是否足以支撐此前大幅拉升的估值。
市場開始認知，雲端業者資本支出不可能永久維持高速成長。當產業從快速擴張期進入高檔成長階段，資本支出增速放緩，過去依賴「AI 投資越多、供應鏈越受惠」的估值模式也必須調整。這也是美光、鎧俠與 SK 海力士等記憶體股即使財報亮眼，仍遭遇賣壓的原因。
AI 商業模式核心轉向「收租能力」
市場重新看好 CSP 業者，關鍵在於投資人開始重新計算 AI 基礎設施的投資報酬率。摩根士丹利測算，在 GPU 租賃模式下，投資資本報酬率（ROIC）約 31%，若 GPU 利用率提升、租賃價格上升，ROIC 甚至可進一步提高。這顯示重資產投入不代表低報酬，雲端業者反而可能透過長期基礎設施形成穩定收益。
此外，資料中心土地、電力與機房等核心資產使用周期可超過 30 年，並能支援多代伺服器升級，使早期投入基礎建設的 CSP 業者具備長期經濟效益。
市場也開始區分不同 AI 商業模式的報酬能力。單純 GPU 租賃模式 ROIC 約 31%，自有基礎設施上的模型 API 模式約 46%，而使用第三方算力的模型 API 模式僅約 25%，顯示掌握算力與分發渠道的平台更具優勢。
模型降價削弱議價權 雲端平台反而受益
AI 產業另一項重大變化，是模型價格戰正在加速。文件指出，OpenAI 近期大幅降低模型價格，反映開源模型競爭正在削弱閉源模型過去的定價能力。中國開源模型在 API 平台上的使用占比快速提升，使模型服務逐漸走向商品化。
當模型從稀缺資源轉變為標準化商品，市場議價權開始回流至掌握算力、客戶與分發渠道的平台。CSP 業者可同時提供 GPU 租賃、自託管模型與自研 AI 服務，成為不同模型與企業需求之間的整合平台。
這也意味著，未來 AI 產業的最大受益者，可能不再只是最強模型開發商，而是能有效配置算力、串聯多元模型並透過用量收費的平台企業。
AI 投資進入「證明題」時代
此次市場分化並非代表 AI 熱潮結束，而是投資邏輯正在改變。雲端業者仍受惠於企業 AI 需求擴張，微軟、AWS 與 Google Cloud 營收持續加速，但市場已不再單純獎勵資本支出增加，而是要求企業證明投資能轉化為收入、利潤與現金流。
對 CSP 而言，長期合約、生產級 AI 應用與企業客戶擴散，使「算力出租」具備收租模式的特徵。相較之下，基礎設施供應鏈則面臨更高挑戰，市場開始檢視企業是否過度依賴雲端資本支出的高速成長，以及估值是否已提前反映未來數年的樂觀預期。
未來 AI 產業鏈的勝負關鍵，將取決於三項因素：產品升級速度、是否過度依賴遠期成長預期，以及收入、獲利與現金流能否相互驗證。市場不再只關注誰站在 AI 浪潮上，而是尋找真正能從浪潮中持續創造現金流的企業。
paras_en: The AI investment boom is reaching a new watershed. Recent U.S. tech earnings season shows a clear split: cloud service providers (CSPs) such as Microsoft (MSFT-US) and Amazon (AMZN-US) saw their stocks surge to record highs, while AI infrastructure suppliers like SK Hynix (000660KS) and Kioxia suffered steep declines, with some memory stocks halving. The market is re‑evaluating who truly benefits from the AI wave, shifting focus from "who is pouring in the most capital" to "who can turn that investment into cash flow".

Over the past two years, the market chased the logic of expanding AI infrastructure: as cloud giants raised capital expenditures (CapEx), the whole supply chain—GPUs, HBM, optical interconnects, switches, PCBs, power supplies and data centers—benefited in tandem. Now investors are asking tougher questions: where does massive AI spending end up as revenue, and whose balance sheets will bear the resulting depreciation costs?
A new consensus is forming: AI money isn’t disappearing; it’s moving from "the shovel sellers" to "the shovel users who create business models".

Cloud giants prove AI demand is turning into revenue. A key signal of the market’s re‑pricing comes from cloud providers showing stronger AI monetisation. Microsoft Azure’s Q2 revenue grew 43% YoY, Amazon AWS rose 37% YoY—its fastest pace in 18 quarters—and Google Cloud jumped 82% YoY, bringing the three major clouds to a combined annualised cloud revenue of $389 billion.

More importantly, AI demand is no longer limited to a handful of frontier model companies. Microsoft disclosed commercial remaining performance obligations (RPO) of $678 billion, up 84% YoY, with new demand coming mainly from banks, manufacturers, healthcare and government customers, indicating AI applications are gradually permeating core enterprise processes.

Amazon AWS also revealed that enterprise customers are signing multi‑year commitment contracts, with demand still outstripping supply. The market sees long‑term contracts as evidence that AI compute demand has moved from testing to full commercial deployment, giving cloud providers a more stable revenue outlook.

Infrastructure chain faces valuation re‑pricing. In contrast, AI infrastructure suppliers are undergoing a sharp correction. SK Hynix posted its strongest earnings ever, with operating profit up 557%, yet its stock fell sharply; the market now cares not just about growth, but whether growth is fast enough to justify the lofty valuations that were previously applied.

Investors are recognising that cloud providers cannot sustain ultra‑high CapEx forever. As the industry shifts from a rapid‑expansion phase to a high‑single‑digit growth stage, CapEx growth slows, and the old valuation model—"more AI spend, more supply‑chain benefit"—must be adjusted. This explains why memory stocks such as Micron, Kioxia and SK Hynix, despite bright earnings, still face selling pressure.

The core of AI business models is shifting to "rent‑collecting ability". The market’s renewed favour for CSPs stems from investors recalculating the return on AI infrastructure investment. Morgan Stanley estimates that under a GPU‑leasing model, the return on invested capital (ROIC) is about 31%; if GPU utilisation rises and lease prices increase, ROIC could climb even higher, showing that heavy‑asset spending does not necessarily mean low returns, and cloud providers can generate stable income through long‑term infrastructure.

Furthermore, core assets such as data‑center land, power and facilities have useful lives exceeding 30 years and can support multiple generations of server upgrades, giving early‑investing CSPs long‑term economic benefits.

The market also begins to differentiate the reward potential of various AI business models. Pure GPU‑leasing yields an ROIC of roughly 31%, a model‑API offering on owned infrastructure about 46%, while a model‑API that relies on third‑party compute is only around 25%, indicating platforms that control both compute and distribution channels have a clear advantage.

Model price cuts erode bargaining power, while cloud platforms benefit. Another major shift is an accelerating price war among AI models. Documents show OpenAI recently slashed model prices dramatically, reflecting that open‑source competition is weakening the pricing power of proprietary models. Chinese open‑source models are rapidly gaining share on API platforms, turning model services into commodities.

As models move from scarce resources to standardized products, bargaining power shifts back to platforms that own compute, customers and distribution channels. CSPs can simultaneously offer GPU leasing, self‑hosted models and proprietary AI services, becoming integration hubs between diverse models and enterprise needs.

This means the biggest future beneficiaries of the AI industry may no longer be the strongest model developers, but the platform companies that can efficiently allocate compute, stitch together multiple models and charge based on usage.

AI investment enters a "proof" era. This market split does not signal the end of the AI hype; it signals a change in investment logic. Cloud providers continue to benefit from expanding enterprise AI demand, with Microsoft, AWS and Google Cloud revenues accelerating, but the market now rewards not just higher CapEx but proof that investments translate into revenue, profit and cash flow.

For CSPs, long‑term contracts, production‑grade AI applications and broad enterprise adoption give "compute renting" the characteristics of a rent‑collecting model. In contrast, the infrastructure supply chain faces tougher challenges, as investors scrutinise whether companies are overly reliant on fast‑growing cloud CapEx and whether valuations have already baked in overly optimistic multi‑year expectations.

The future winners in the AI value chain will hinge on three factors: speed of product upgrades, dependence on far‑future growth assumptions, and whether revenue, profit and cash flow can validate each other. The market is no longer only looking for who stands on the AI wave, but for companies that can continuously generate cash flow from it.

items.title: AI晶片掀史上最大融資潮？Citadel：科技巨頭2028年前恐發債逾5000億美元
items.title_en: AI Chip Frenzy: Citadel Warns of Historic Debt Wave, Tech Giants May Issue Over $50 Trillion by 2028
paras: 全球信貸市場才剛消化完數據中心建設帶來的巨額舉債潮，一波規模更龐大的融資壓力恐怕已在路上，恐將改寫整個投資級信用市場的生態。
根據做市商 Citadel Securities 的最新研判，美國科技巨頭爲了持續採購 AI 晶片，未來到 2028 年之間，恐將透過公開及私募市場合計舉債超過 5000 億美元。
Citadel 投資級信用研究主管 Jeff Eason 直言，這波即將到來的融資潮「相對於現有市場規模而言可說史無前例」，而且他強調，這個預估數字很可能還算是相對保守的估計。
Eason 分析，若 5000 億美元的預測成真，屆時這筆金額將占彭博美國投資級指數逾 5% 的比重。
換句話說，投資人恐怕得被迫調整既有配置，縮減在科技、媒體與電信類股的持倉，才能挪出空間來承接這波晶片融資債券的供給。
事實上，全球信用市場先前已消化了約 5700 億美元與 AI 相關的舉債，主要由亞馬遜 (AMZN-US) 、微軟 (MSFT-US) 、Alphabet(GOOGL-US) 旗下 Google 等「超大規模雲端運算商」發行，用於支撐數據中心的擴建工程。
單是美國市場，去年以來就吸納了大約 600 億美元、期限最長五年的短天期債務。
但 Eason 警告，這些數字放到晶片融資的需求面前，恐怕都要相形見絀。他估算，光是 2028 年單一年度，晶片製造商的債務發行規模就可能突破 2500 億美元。
他說：「投資人根本還沒經歷過這種等級的融資衝擊。」
從結構面來看，Eason 預期這波晶片相關債務多半會落在三到五年的中短期限，原因在於這樣的天期較貼近晶片本身的使用週期；部分發行也可能透過 144A 私募規則進行。
這代表，市場勢必得在相對集中的時間內，消化一波接一波的大量供給。
近來包括 Anthropic 在內的 AI 業者，已展現出對多元化債務工具的高度依賴。Anthropic 今年稍早完成一筆規模約 350 億美元的融資安排，用途正是購買 Google 客製化的 TPU 晶片，這筆交易也被視爲私募信貸史上數一數二的大案。
值得注意的是，博通爲這筆債務的高順位優先級部分提供信用背書，讓華爾街各大銀行得以將相關債權份額在市場上流通轉手。
另一家 AI 巨頭 OpenAI 同樣現金消耗速度驚人，爲了維持業務規模擴張，該公司也愈來愈仰賴大型機構提供的債務支持與擔保機制，藉此打通市場融資管道。
Citadel 自 2024 年初跨入投資級信用市場，據公司全球信用交易主管 Sam Berberian 透露，去年公司在這塊業務的名義交易量已達到約 5000 億美元規模。
Eason 與團隊成員、投資級信用分析師 Tucker Roberts 共同認爲，晶片融資債券一旦大舉湧入市場，很可能催生出投資級信用市場前所未見的全新基準板塊，進而牽動信用利差走勢、投資組合佈局邏輯，乃至整個 AI 產業鏈的資本配置方式。
Eason 總結指出：「這已經不只是融資規模的問題，它很可能從根本上改變投資級市場的組成樣貌。」
paras_en: The global credit market is still digesting the massive debt wave from data center construction, but a new, even larger wave of financing pressure is looming, potentially rewriting the entire investment-grade credit market ecosystem.

According to Citadel Securities' latest analysis, US tech giants will likely issue over $50 trillion in debt between now and 2028 to continue purchasing AI chips, a scale that is unprecedented compared to the current market.

Jeff Eason, head of investment-grade credit research at Citadel, said that this upcoming wave of financing is 'unprecedented in terms of market size' and that the estimated $50 trillion figure may be a conservative estimate.
Eason analyzed that if the $50 trillion prediction comes true, this amount would account for over 5% of the Bloomberg US Investment-Grade Index.
In other words, investors may have to adjust their existing allocations, reducing their holdings in tech, media, and telecom stocks to make room for the influx of chip-related debt securities.

In fact, the global credit market has already absorbed around $5.7 trillion in debt related to AI, mainly from Amazon (AMZN-US), Microsoft (MSFT-US), Alphabet (GOOGL-US) subsidiary Google, and other 'super-scale cloud computing companies' that issued debt to support data center expansion projects.
In the US market alone, around $60 billion in short-term debt has been absorbed since last year, with maturities of up to five years.
However, Eason warned that these numbers pale in comparison to the demand for chip financing. He estimates that chip manufacturers may issue over $250 billion in debt alone in 2028.
He said, 'Investors haven't experienced this level of financing impact yet.'

From a structural perspective, Eason expects most of the chip-related debt to fall within the three- to five-year medium- to short-term horizon, as this aligns with the usage cycle of the chips themselves. Some issuances may also be made under the 144A private placement rules.
This means that the market will have to digest a large influx of supply in a relatively concentrated period.

Recent AI players, including Anthropic, have shown a high reliance on diversified debt instruments. Anthropic recently completed a $35 billion financing arrangement to purchase customized TPU chips from Google, a transaction that is considered one of the largest private credit deals in history.
Notably, Broadcom provided credit backing for the high-priority portion of the debt, allowing major banks on Wall Street to securitize and trade the related debt securities.
Another AI giant, OpenAI, has also shown a rapid cash burn rate, relying increasingly on large institutions to provide debt support and guarantee mechanisms to access the market.

Citadel, which entered the investment-grade credit market in early 2024, reported that its global credit trading volume reached around $50 trillion last year, according to Sam Berberian, global credit trading head.

Eason and his team, including investment-grade credit analyst Tucker Roberts, believe that the influx of chip financing debt securities will likely create a new, unprecedented benchmark segment in the investment-grade credit market, driving credit spreads, investment portfolio logic, and capital allocation in the entire AI industry chain.
Eason concluded, 'This is no longer just a matter of financing scale; it may fundamentally change the composition of the investment-grade market.'

items.title: Google表外擔保暴增至438億美元！豪賭AI、換取TPU銷售動能
items.title_en: Google’s Off‑Balance‑Sheet Guarantees Surge to $43.8 B! Betting Big on AI to Boost TPU Sales
paras: 在人工智慧（AI）軍備競賽白熱化之際，Google 母公司 Alphabet(GOOGL-US) 正悄悄向華爾街的金融工程借力，用一套過去鮮少出現在科技巨頭身上的手法，即透過大規模表外擔保，來為自研 AI 晶片鋪路。
根據 Alphabet 最新揭露的財報資訊，該公司為資料中心租戶提供的潛在違約擔保，其「名目金額」已從去年九月底的 65 億美元，一口氣暴增近六倍，來到 438 億美元。
這也代表，一旦擔保對象出現財務問題，Google 最壞情況下可能需要承擔的支付責任，已達到數百億美元等級。

用擔保換市占：TPU 對抗輝達的另一條路

根據《The Information》報導，這波擔保潮的背後，是 Google 推廣自家張量處理器（TPU）的野心。
相較於輝達 (NVDA-US) 的 AI 晶片，TPU 若要打入更多資料中心與客戶（例如 Anthropic），往往需要開發商能以較低成本取得融資。
而 Google 提供的財務擔保，正好能替這些資料中心開發商增加信用背書，讓他們更容易借到便宜的錢、加快機房興建速度。
換言之，Google 正用自己的資產負債表當作籌碼，以換取 TPU 在市場上的擴張空間。
知情人士向媒體透露，Google 內部評估後認為，未來 TPU 銷售所帶來的營收，將遠遠超過這些擔保可能造成的財務負擔，高層對這筆帳相當有信心。
目前，Google 已針對約十個資料中心專案、合計約 2.4 吉瓦的電力容量提供了擔保，不過由於相關工程都還沒完工，這些擔保實際上尚未啟動。
值得留意的是，這類交易多半有固定的三角結構：雲端新創公司 Fluidstack 負責承租與規劃資料中心，並在裡面裝設 TPU，再將運算力轉租給 Anthropic 等終端使用者。
而 Hut 8 (HUT-US) 、TeraWulf (WULF-US) 這類原本從事加密貨幣挖礦、如今轉型投入 AI 基礎設施的業者，則常是資料中心的實際營運方。

帳面數字看似驚人 實際風險受控？

儘管 438 億美元的名目擔保金額十分嚇人，但真正記錄在 Alphabet 資產負債表上的公允價值，其實只有 8.15 億美元。
這是因為「名目價值」代表的是最極端情境下的最大可能損失，而公允價值才是 Google 根據違約機率、違約時間點與可回收金額等假設，估算出的實際預期支出。
信評機構 CreditSights 技術研究主管 Jordan Chalfin 指出，外界不需要對這個名目數字過度緊張，因為有多重機制能緩解風險。
舉例來說，若租戶違約，Google 通常有權接手底層的租約，自行使用或轉租給其他客戶，等於變相取得了稀缺的運算容量；再加上許多租約長達十五年，潛在的風險敞口會隨時間逐步遞減。
Fitch Ratings 信用分析師 Anubhav Arora 則坦言，評等機構之所以願意給這些資料中心專案投資等級評等，「高度仰賴 Google 提供的擔保」作為信用支撐。
他預期這股趨勢短期內不會停歇，畢竟 Google 過去十二個月的營運現金流超過 1850 億美元，融資實力仍相當雄厚。

資產負債表大變身：從「零負債」神話到近千億美元舉債

Alphabet 長年給外界的印象，是現金水位極高、幾乎不需要靠負債擴張的穩健企業。然而，這樣的形象正快速瓦解。
截至六月底，Alphabet 的債務規模已從一年前的 236 億美元，暴增至 980 億美元；公司並在二十多年來首次發行新股籌資。上季財報更顯示，Alphabet 作為上市公司，史上首度出現自由現金流為負的季度。
除了已生效的 438 億美元擔保外，Alphabet 另外還簽下總額 852 億美元、尚未正式啟動的表外資料中心租賃合約；為協助合作夥伴取得電力與能源設備，又額外提供了 76 億美元的後備擔保，並已承諾在條款拍板後，再追加 241 億美元的未來擔保額度。
分析人士指出，這股靠表外工具支撐 AI 建設的風潮並非 Google 獨有。Meta(META-US) 透過在路易斯安那州、德州成立少數股權合資企業，把資料中心建設成本移出自家資產負債表。
此外，甲骨文 (ORCL-US) 同樣仰賴類似的表外安排來支應擴張野心。AI 基礎設施的燒錢速度，正迫使科技巨頭們一齊向華爾街的融資手法靠攏。

提供擔保也要分一杯羹：認股權證鎖住上檔獲利

有趣的是，Google 在承擔下檔風險的同時，也沒忘記為自己爭取上檔利益。
在部分交易中，Google 會以提供擔保為條件，向資料中心開發商換取股權認股權證。換言之，若這些公司股價表現亮眼，Google 也能跟著受惠。
例如，在紐約州巴克為 Fluidstack 興建資料中心的 TeraWulf，Google 握有的認股權證相當於該公司 14% 股權；在與 Cipher Digital 的合作案中，Google 也取得價值相當於 5.4% 股權的認股權證。
一旦 Google 選擇提前終止擔保，雖然可能得向債券持有人支付一大筆一次性費用，但這筆錢實質上會轉化為對該專案的所有權權益。
不過並非所有交易都如此對等。以 Hut 8 的合作案為例，Fitch Ratings 指出，若 Fluidstack 違約，Google 必須概括承受長達十五年租期的全部付款義務，而且一旦工程出現重大延誤，雙方都無法片面解除合約。
更特別的是，Google 在這筆交易中並未取得任何認股權證。Hut 8 執行長 Asher Genoot 在財報電話會議上透露，這筆資料中心租約總價值達 70 億美元，另加約 20 億美元的電力與財產稅保險等費用。
知情人士表示，這筆交易條件特殊，外界普遍認為未來不太可能複製。
paras_en: As the AI arms race heats up, Alphabet (GOOGL-US), Google’s parent, is quietly tapping Wall Street’s financial engineering, using a technique rarely seen at tech giants: massive off‑balance‑sheet guarantees to pave the way for its own AI chips.

According to Alphabet’s latest disclosed financials, the potential default guarantees it provides to data‑center tenants have a "nominal amount" that jumped from $6.5 billion at the end of September last year to nearly six times that, reaching $43.8 billion.
That means, if a guaranteed party runs into financial trouble, Google could be on the hook for payments in the hundreds of billions of dollars in a worst‑case scenario.
Using Guarantees to Gain Market Share: TPU’s Alternative Path Against Nvidia
The wave of guarantees, reported by The Information, is driven by Google’s ambition to push its own Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).
Compared with Nvidia’s (NVDA-US) AI chips, TPUs need developers to obtain financing at lower cost in order to win more data‑centers and customers such as Anthropic.
Google’s financial guarantees give those data‑center developers a credit endorsement, making it easier for them to borrow cheap money and speed up facility construction.
In other words, Google is using its balance sheet as a bargaining chip to expand TPU market reach.

Insiders told the media that internal assessments show future TPU‑related revenue will far outweigh any financial burden from the guarantees, and senior management is very confident about the accounting line.

So far Google has provided guarantees for about ten data‑center projects covering roughly 2.4 GW of power capacity, but because the projects are not yet completed, the guarantees have not been triggered.

These deals typically follow a triangular structure: the cloud‑startup Fluidstack leases and plans the data center, installs TPUs inside, and then sub‑leases compute capacity to end users such as Anthropic.
Companies that originally mined cryptocurrency, such as Hut 8 (HUT-US) and TeraWulf (WULF-US), have pivoted to AI infrastructure and often act as the actual operators of the data centers.
The headline figure of $43.8 billion looks alarming, but the fair‑value amount recorded on Alphabet’s balance sheet is only $815 million.

The "nominal value" reflects the maximum possible loss in an extreme scenario, whereas fair value is the expected outflow Google estimates based on default probability, timing and recoverable amounts.
Credit‑rating firm CreditSights’ technical research head Jordan Chalfin says the market need not overreact to the nominal number because multiple mechanisms mitigate risk.

For example, if a tenant defaults, Google usually has the right to take over the underlying lease, use the space itself or re‑lease it to another customer, effectively acquiring scarce compute capacity; many leases run up to fifteen years, so exposure diminishes over time.

Fitch Ratings analyst Anubhav Arora notes that rating agencies are willing to give these data‑center projects investment‑grade ratings largely because of the “highly relied‑upon” guarantees from Google.
He expects the trend to continue in the short term, given Alphabet’s operating cash flow of over $185 billion in the past twelve months, which shows strong financing capacity.
Balance‑Sheet Transformation: From a "Zero‑Debt" Myth to Nearly $100 Billion of Borrowing
Alphabet has long cultivated an image of a cash‑rich, virtually debt‑free, ultra‑stable company, but that perception is rapidly eroding.

As of the end of June, Alphabet’s debt rose from $23.6 billion a year ago to $98 billion, and the company issued new equity for the first time in more than two decades. Its most recent quarterly report even showed a negative free‑cash‑flow quarter for the first time in history.

In addition to the $43.8 billion of guarantees already in effect, Alphabet has signed off‑balance‑sheet data‑center lease contracts totaling $85.2 billion that have not yet been activated; it also provided a $7.6 billion backup guarantee to help partners secure power and equipment, and has pledged an additional $24.1 billion of future guarantees once the terms are finalized.

Analysts point out that this wave of off‑balance‑sheet tools to fund AI builds is not unique to Google. Meta (META-US) has created minority‑equity joint ventures in Louisiana and Texas to move data‑center construction costs off its own balance sheet.

Oracle (ORCL-US) similarly relies on comparable off‑balance‑sheet arrangements to fund its expansion ambitions. The cash‑burn rate of AI infrastructure is pushing the tech giants toward Wall Street‑style financing.
Guarantees Also Earn a Slice of the Upside: Warrants Lock In Potential Gains
Interestingly, while Google assumes downside risk, it also secures upside upside by extracting equity‑linked warrants in some transactions.
In certain deals, Google provides guarantees in exchange for stock warrants from the data‑center developers. If those companies’ shares perform well, Google benefits as well.

For example, in the TeraWulf data‑center that Fluidstack is building in Buck, New York, Google holds warrants equivalent to 14 % of the company’s equity; in its partnership with Cipher Digital, Google obtained warrants representing roughly 5.4 % of the equity.
If Google chooses to terminate a guarantee early, it may have to pay a large one‑time fee to bondholders, but that payment effectively converts into an ownership stake in the project.

However, not all transactions are structured that way. In the Hut 8 deal, Fitch Ratings notes that if Fluidstack defaults, Google would have to assume the full payment obligations for the entire fifteen‑year lease, and any major construction delay would prevent either party from unilaterally walking away.

Moreover, Google did not receive any warrants in that particular transaction. Hut 8 CEO Asher Genoot told the earnings call that the data‑center lease is valued at $7 billion, plus roughly $2 billion in power, property‑tax and insurance costs.
Insiders say the terms of that deal are unique and unlikely to be replicated elsewhere.

items.title: 美AI股反彈動能本周迎「硬門檻」！華爾街估7月非農就業新增8.5萬人 Kalshi押7萬區間
items.title_en: US AI Stocks Face "Hard Threshold" This Week as Wall Street Expects 850,000 July Non-Farm Payroll Additions
paras: 美國勞工統計局 (BLS) 本週五 (7 日) 將公布 7 月非農就業新增人數，道瓊斯經濟學家一致預期新增 8.5 萬人、失業率 4.3%，《路透社》調查中位數落在 8.3-8.5 萬人，巴克莱等樂觀派看 10 萬，相較於 6 月僅增 5.7 萬、失業率 4.2%，市場實質押注「低成長但未失速」的溫和放緩。
對全球股票多頭、尤其半導體與 AI 算力鏈而言，週五數據是 7 月底暴力反彈後第一道硬門檻。6 月非農就業人數爆冷至僅新增 5.7 萬人後，「升息預期降溫」讓那指與費半指數獲得喘息機會。
最理想情境是新增 7 萬至 10 萬人、失業率穩在 4.2% 至 4.3%、薪資續降的「金髮姑娘」組合，既證明消費與企業獲利未滑向衰退，又不逼聯準會 (Fed) 強化升息路徑，壓低實質利率與折現率，這對長期、估值敏感的 HBM、網通與 AI 應用股屬於利多。
但付費預測市場搶跑華爾街。Kalshi 與 Polymarket 真金白銀押注者認為，7 月新增逾 8 萬人機率僅 47%、超 7 萬人約 60%、達 9 萬人約 41%、破 10 萬人略高於三分之一，不到 6 萬人機率約三分之一。
Kalshi 上月曾押注 6 月超 12.5 萬機率 63%，結果最終 5.7 萬，預測盤同樣看走眼。
不過，若新增破 10 萬人且薪資增幅重新加速，聯準會 9 月升息機率 (當前約 64% 至 68%) 與長債殖利率回彈，30 年期美債曾觸 5.24% 至 5.27%，高估值 AI 股吃不下第二輪利率衝擊。
若低於 6 萬人且失業率彈升、工時萎縮，債市初步上漲後邏輯會切至「獲利衰退」，週期、金融、出口鏈將先受到影響。
油價周一 (3 日) 收跌約 5%、美債殖利率回落帶動標普 500 指數收漲 1.48%、那指漲 2.13%，多頭依賴的正是「油價降＋利率降＋科技獲利韌性」三大利多共振。
專家指出，非農數據不是單一利多，而是把 7 月槓桿強平後的技術修復，升格為新一輪風險偏好上行、或是打回高波動回補的分水嶺。
paras_en: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is set to release the July non-farm payroll additions on Friday, with Wall Street economists unanimously expecting an addition of 850,000 jobs and a 4.3% unemployment rate. A Reuters survey puts the median estimate at 830,000 to 850,000, while Barclays and other optimistic analysts predict 1 million additions, compared to the 570,000 additions in June and a 4.2% unemployment rate. The market is essentially betting on a "soft landing" with moderate growth but no slowdown.

For global stock bulls, particularly those in the semiconductor and AI computing chains, Friday's data will be the first "hard threshold" since the violent rebound at the end of July. After the June non-farm payroll additions came in at a disappointing 570,000, "dovish" expectations of interest rate hikes gave the Nasdaq and the Philly Fed Index a breather.

The ideal scenario would be an addition of 700,000 to 1 million jobs, a stable unemployment rate of 4.2% to 4.3%, and a decline in wages, which would prove that consumption and corporate profits have not yet slid into a recession, while also not forcing the Federal Reserve (Fed) to strengthen its interest rate hike path, thereby lowering the effective interest rate and discount rate. This would be a positive for long-term, value-sensitive stocks in HBM, telecom, and AI applications.

However, paid prediction markets are beating Wall Street to the punch. Kalshi and Polymarket's silver-tongued bettors believe that the probability of adding over 800,000 jobs is only 47%, while exceeding 700,000 jobs is around 60%, reaching 900,000 jobs is approximately 41%, and breaking 1 million jobs is slightly above one-third. The probability of adding less than 600,000 jobs is around one-third.
Kalshi had previously bet on a 63% probability of exceeding 12.5 million jobs in June, but the actual number came in at 570,000, with the prediction market also looking over-optimistic.

However, if the additions exceed 1 million and wages growth accelerates, the Fed's interest rate hike probability in September (currently around 64% to 68%) and the long-term bond yield will rebound, with the 30-year US Treasury yield touching 5.24% to 5.27%, which would be a second-round shock for high-valued AI stocks.

If the additions are below 600,000 and the unemployment rate rises, with hours worked declining, the bond market will initially rally before logic shifts to "profit decline," with cyclicals, financials, and export chains being the first to be affected.

Oil prices fell by around 5% on Monday, with the 10-year Treasury yield decline driving the S&P 500 index up 1.48% and the Nasdaq up 2.13%, with bulls relying on the "oil price down + interest rate down + tech profit resilience" triple bullish synergy.

Experts point out that non-farm payroll data is not a single bullish factor, but rather a technical repair of the July 7th strong flattening, which has been upgraded to a new round of risk-on, or a dividing line for high volatility to rebound.

items.title: 蘋果20週年大改版！iPhone 20傳採玻璃超薄機身 散熱再升級
items.title_en: Apple 20th Anniversary iPhone 20 Rumored to Feature Glass Body and Improved Cooling
paras: 蘋果傳出計畫在 2027 年底推出 iPhone 問世 20 週年紀念機型，市場暫稱「iPhone 20」。最新消息指出，這款新機可能大量採用玻璃材質，並借鑑 iPhone Air 的超薄設計，同時擴大機身內部的散熱空間，以兼顧輕薄外型與效能表現。
微博爆料帳號「定焦數碼」近日表示，iPhone 20 的機身將以玻璃為主要材料，中框設計則可能接近 iPhone Air，整體厚度也有望維持在相近水準。
過去相關傳聞曾指出，蘋果可能為這款紀念機導入大面積曲面玻璃及固態按鍵，進一步減少傳統機械結構，打造更一體化的外觀。
這並非「定焦數碼」首次將 iPhone 20 與 iPhone Air 相提並論。該帳號 7 月便曾透露，蘋果準備讓週年紀念機型「回歸玻璃」，部分零組件可能沿用第一代 iPhone Air 採用的加工方式。
除了外觀變化，iPhone 20 的散熱能力也可能升級。
「定焦數碼」聲稱，新機內部的散熱板將擴大約「1 吋」，暗示蘋果可能為這款超薄機型配置面積更大的導熱結構，藉此提升長時間執行高負載工作的穩定性。
目前尚無法確定 iPhone 20 是否會直接採用均熱板散熱。
iPhone 17 Pro 系列已導入均熱板技術，可將 A19 Pro 晶片產生的熱量快速分散至機身其他區域；定位更輕薄的 iPhone Air 則未採用相同方案。
考量超薄機身通常更難處理熱量，蘋果 (AAPL-US) 若要進一步提升紀念機型的性能，導入均熱板具有一定合理性。
同一爆料來源先前也曾宣稱，折疊式 iPhone 將配置多組均熱板。不過，所謂散熱板面積增加，也可能只是代表蘋果擴大傳統導熱材料，而非確定採用均熱板。
蘋果 (AAPL-US) 週一 (3 日) 下滑約 1.8%，收在 303.42 美元，連續第四個交易日收黑，由於 Alphabet (GOOGL-US) 市值超越蘋果，使蘋果跌至全美市值第三大企業。
paras_en: Apple is reportedly planning to release a 20th-anniversary iPhone model, dubbed 'iPhone 20,' in late 2027. According to the latest rumors, this new device may feature a glass body and adopt the ultra-thin design of the iPhone Air, while also expanding the internal cooling space to balance the lightweight exterior and performance.

A Weibo account called '定焦數碼' (Ding Jiao Shu Mu) recently claimed that the iPhone 20's body will be made of glass, with a middle frame design similar to the iPhone Air, and a thickness that may be similar to the Air.

Previous rumors suggested that Apple might introduce large-area curved glass and solid-state buttons for this commemorative model, further reducing traditional mechanical structures and creating a more integrated appearance.

This is not the first time '定焦數碼' has compared the iPhone 20 to the iPhone Air. The account revealed in July that Apple plans to let the anniversary model 'return to glass,' with some components possibly using the same processing method as the first-generation iPhone Air.
In addition to the exterior changes, the iPhone 20's cooling capabilities may also be upgraded.

'定焦數碼' claims that the new device's heat sink will be expanded by about '1 inch,' implying that Apple may equip this ultra-thin model with a larger heat-dissipation structure to improve stability during long periods of high-load work.
It is currently unclear whether the iPhone 20 will directly adopt the uniform heat plate cooling system.

The iPhone 17 Pro series has already introduced uniform heat plate technology, which quickly disperses heat generated by the A19 Pro chip to other areas of the device; in contrast, the thinner iPhone Air does not use the same scheme.

Considering that ultra-thin devices often have difficulty handling heat, Apple (AAPL-US) may have a rational reason to introduce uniform heat plates to further improve the performance of the commemorative model.

The same leak source previously claimed that the foldable iPhone would be equipped with multiple uniform heat plates. However, the increased heat sink area may simply represent Apple expanding traditional heat-dissipation materials rather than adopting uniform heat plates.

Apple (AAPL-US) fell by about 1.8% on Monday (3rd) to close at $303.42, marking its fourth consecutive trading day in the red. As Alphabet (GOOGL-US) surpassed Apple in market value, Apple dropped to the third-largest company in the US by market value.

items.title: 輝達卡關200美元區間 科技巨頭財報也未能助突破
items.title_en: Nvidia Stuck in $200 Range, Tech Giants' Earnings Also Fail to Break Through
paras: 《巴隆周刊》報導，輝達 (Nvidia)(NVDA-US) 股價周一 (3 日) 收高，扭轉盤中早些時候跌勢。不過，這家晶片大廠的股價似乎仍需要一份亮眼的財報，才能真正擺脫目前的盤整格局。
輝達股價終場上漲 2.9%，收在 206.64 美元，盤中一度漲至 208.74 美元。但過去三個月來，股價大致呈現橫盤整理，累計僅上漲 1.1%。
截至目前，本季財報季尚未為輝達帶來明顯催化劑。雖然多家科技巨頭陸續上調資本支出預測，但市場開始質疑，輝達是否仍會是最大受惠者，因記憶體晶片等其他 AI 硬體成本持續攀升，可能分食原本流向 GPU 的投資預算。
更大的問題在於，整體 AI 投資熱潮正受到借貸成本上升的影響而出現降溫跡象，使輝達股價難以持續突破。
此外，輝達近期透過資產負債表向 AI 新創企業提供融資的做法——《巴隆》形容其如「同時扮演創投與中央銀行」——也引發市場質疑。
21Shares 宏觀經濟研究主管 Stephen Coltman 在報告中表示，「許多過去現金流極為充沛的企業，如今為了投資 AI 基礎設施，不得不大舉舉債。即使是獲利能力最高、市值最大的輝達，也因傳出向客戶提供數千億美元規模的供應商融資與信用擔保，導致其信用利差擴大。」
不過，市場仍期待輝達將於 8 月 26 日公布的財報，有望成為股價突破盤整的重要催化劑，前提是投資人認為目前股價已具備足夠吸引力。
根據 FactSet，目前華爾街分析師對輝達的平均目標價為 314.29 美元。
今年以來，輝達股價累計上漲 10.8%，若以過去 12 個月計算，漲幅則達 14.8%。
paras_en: Baron Weekly reported that Nvidia (NVDA-US) shares closed higher on Monday (the 3rd), reversing an earlier intraday decline. However, the chip maker still seems to need a standout earnings report to truly escape its current consolidation pattern.
Nvidia’s stock finished up 2.9% at $206.64, having peaked intraday at $208.74. Over the past three months the stock has essentially moved sideways, gaining only 1.1% in total.

So far this earnings season has not provided a clear catalyst for Nvidia. Although several tech giants have been raising their capital‑expenditure forecasts, the market is beginning to question whether Nvidia will remain the biggest beneficiary, as costs for other AI hardware such as memory chips continue to rise and could eat into the budget that would otherwise go to GPUs.
A bigger issue is that the overall AI investment boom is showing signs of cooling as borrowing costs rise, making it harder for Nvidia’s share price to sustain a breakout.

In addition, Nvidia’s recent practice of providing financing to AI startups through its balance sheet—described by Baron as “playing both venture capitalist and central bank”—has also drawn market skepticism.

Stephen Coltman, head of macro‑economic research at 21Shares, said in a report, “Many companies that once had abundant cash flow now have to take on large debt to invest in AI infrastructure. Even the most profitable and largest‑by‑market‑cap company, Nvidia, has seen its credit spread widen after reports that it is offering supplier financing and credit guarantees to customers worth hundreds of billions of dollars.”

Nevertheless, the market still hopes that Nvidia’s earnings report due on August 26 will serve as a key catalyst for breaking out of the range, provided investors deem the current price sufficiently attractive.
According to FactSet, Wall Street analysts currently have an average target price of $314.29 for Nvidia.
So far this year Nvidia’s stock has risen 10.8%, and over the past 12 months it has gained 14.8%.

items.title: 股價較高點回跌逾4成！SpaceX首份財報將掀牌 AI、星鏈、星艦受檢驗
items.title_en: Stock Falls Over 40% From Recent Highs! SpaceX's First Earnings Report to Spotlight AI, Starlink, Starship Scrutiny
paras: SpaceX(SPCX-US)將於美東時間周二(4日)盤後公布2026會計年度第2季財報，市場預料結果可能引發股價劇烈波動，目前以人工智慧(AI)業務營收、虧損與資本支出這三大數字最受關注。
這家由全球首富馬斯克領軍的公司，目前市值約1.4兆美元，數周前一度高達3兆美元，目前股價仍為2026年預估營收的35倍，使本次財報成為市場焦點。
Cantor Fitzgerald分析師Colin Canfield表示，目前市場預估值分歧極大，「幾乎沒有人真正知道會開出什麼數字」，財報結果可能與市場預期出現相當大的落差。
AI財務數字與展望
SpaceX目前將業務劃分為三大部門，包括：太空(火箭發射與星艦計畫)，連網(星鏈衛星網路)，AI(主要為今年2月併入的xAI業務)。
三者當中，以AI業務最受市場關注，其在2026年第1季營收為8.18億美元，但營業虧損高達25億美元，單季資本支出更達77億美元。
市場將聚焦三項關鍵指標：AI營收是否快速成長，虧損是否收斂，
AI資本支出是否持續擴大。
SpaceX已與Anthropic及Google(GOOGL-US)簽署AI資料中心租賃協議。兩者當中，Google合約尚未開始貢獻營收，Anthropic每月約12.5億美元的租賃合約，則於5、6月逐步放量，但實際認列營收及獲利率仍不明朗。
投資人也將關注SpaceX對今年下半年及2027年AI業務展望，以及利用星鑑部署低成本AI運算衛星的測試時程。
星艦進度、星鏈用戶
星鑑(Starship)於7月完成第13次飛行測試，市場將關注：第14次測試何時進行，以及星鑑的研發支出規模。
SpaceX在第1季的太空事業新增廠房與設備支出約11億美元。
太空部門2025年營收41億美元，營業虧損為6.57億美元。而獵鷹九號(Falcon 9)在第2季的火箭發射約36次，多數為星鏈(Starlink)任務，因此不會認列為太空部門收入，市場預料投資人仍將把焦點放在AI及星鏈，而非火箭發射業務。
星鏈方面，截至第1季季末的全球訂戶已達1030萬戶，較一年前約500萬戶倍增。該項業務在2025年的營收為114億美元，營業利益44億美元。
市場將關注星鏈的訂戶成長速度、每位用戶平均收入(ARPU)，以及
企業及政府客戶訂單。Canfield預期，SpaceX將首度揭露更多有關星鏈的營運指標。
Canfield預期，這份財報將優於市場預期，且全年獲利展望可望上修。
目前華爾街平均預估第2季營收將為69億美元，而稅息折舊及攤銷前利益(EBITDA)為21億美元
全年部分，營收估為390億美元，EBITDA為173億美元。不過市場預估分歧極大。
解禁賣壓仍是股價隱憂
SapceX周一盤中一度跌至每股104.83美元、創上市新低，但終場反彈5.68%，收在每股114.53美元。然而周一收盤價仍比6月16日首次公開發行(IPO)後創下的歷史收盤高點(201.80美元)回跌了43%。
其中一項憂慮來自IPO禁售期即將屆滿。根據規劃，8月6日將有約9.12億股解禁，約一周後另有3.19億股解禁。
市場擔心早期投資人可能趁機獲利了結，對股價形成賣壓。但也有分析認為，市場通常會提前反映已知消息，因此真正解禁後未必再出現新一波拋售。
paras_en: SpaceX (SPCX-US) will release its fiscal 2026 Q2 earnings after market close on Tuesday (the 4th) Eastern Time. The market expects the results could trigger sharp stock volatility, with AI revenue, losses, and capital expenditures being the three most watched figures.

Led by the world’s richest man Elon Musk, the company now has a market value of about $1.4 trillion, after briefly reaching $3 trillion a few weeks ago. Its share price still trades at roughly 35 times the projected 2026 revenue, making this earnings release a focal point for investors.

Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Colin Canfield said market valuation estimates are wildly divergent, "almost nobody really knows what numbers will be reported," and the earnings could differ substantially from expectations.
AI Financial Numbers and Outlook

SpaceX currently groups its operations into three divisions: Space (rocket launches and the Starship program), Connectivity (the Starlink satellite network), and AI (mainly the xAI business that was folded in February this year).

Among them, the AI segment draws the most market attention. It posted Q1 2026 revenue of $818 million but an operating loss of $2.5 billion, and capital expenditures for the quarter reached $7.7 billion.
The market will focus on three key AI metrics: whether AI revenue is growing quickly, whether losses are narrowing, and whether AI capex continues to expand.

SpaceX has signed AI data‑center leasing agreements with Anthropic and Google (GOOGL-US). Google’s contract has not yet contributed revenue, while Anthropic’s lease is about $1.25 billion per month and is expected to ramp up in May and June, though actual recognized revenue and profit margins remain unclear.
Investors will also watch SpaceX’s outlook for AI in the second half of this year and in 2027, as well as the schedule for testing low‑cost AI‑computing satellites deployed via Starship.
Starship Progress and Starlink Users
Starship completed its 13th flight test in July. The market will watch when the 14th test will occur and the scale of R&D spending for Starship.
SpaceX’s Space division recorded roughly $1.1 billion in new plant and equipment spending in Q1.

The Space segment generated $4.1 billion in revenue for 2025 and an operating loss of $657 million. Falcon 9 performed about 36 launches in Q2, most of which were Starlink missions and therefore not counted as Space‑division revenue. Investors are expected to keep their focus on AI and Starlink rather than on launch activity.

For Starlink, global subscriber numbers reached 10.3 million by the end of Q1, roughly double the 5 million a year earlier. The business posted $11.4 billion in revenue and $4.4 billion in operating profit in 2025.

The market will monitor Starlink’s subscriber growth rate, average revenue per user (ARPU), and enterprise and government contracts. Canfield expects SpaceX to disclose more operational metrics for Starlink for the first time.
Canfield anticipates the earnings will beat market expectations and that the full‑year profit outlook could be revised upward.

Wall Street currently forecasts Q2 revenue of $6.9 billion and EBITDA of $2.1 billion. For the full year, revenue is projected at $39 billion with EBITDA of $17.3 billion, though estimates vary widely among analysts.
Unlocking‑related Selling Pressure Remains a Stock Risk

SpaceX’s shares fell intraday on Monday to $104.83, a new low since the company went public, but recovered 5.68% to close at $114.53. Even so, Monday’s close was still 43% below the post‑IPO historical high of $201.80 set on June 16.
One concern stems from the upcoming end of the IPO lock‑up period. About 912 million shares are slated to unlock on August 6, with another 319 million shares scheduled to unlock roughly a week later.

The market worries early investors may seize the chance to cash out, creating selling pressure on the stock. Some analysts, however, argue that markets usually price in known events ahead of time, so a post‑unlock wave of selling may not materialize.

items.title: 【亞股收盤一手掌握】AI概念股震盪整理台股高檔震盪、外資回流南韓，日股關注匯率與債市變化
items.title_en: [Asian Markets Close: One-Handed Overview] AI Concept Stocks Oscillate, Taiwan Index Holds High, Foreign Capital Returns to South Korea, Japan Market Focuses on Yen and Bond Yield Changes
paras: 2026年08月04日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 亞洲股市周二走勢震盪，市場持續消化美國企業財報、AI產業前景及中東局勢等因素。台股盤中一度逼近44,000點整數關卡，但尾盤賣壓出籠，小幅收黑；南韓股市則在槓桿ETF交易降溫後震盪收高，日本股市小幅上漲，市場焦點轉向日圓走勢及公債殖利率變化。
台股今天開低後震盪走高，加權指數盤中最高來到43,912點，一度逼近44,000點，但尾盤賣壓湧現，終場下跌25.75點，收在43,360點，跌幅0.06%，成交值新台幣1兆362億元。
權值股漲跌互見，台積電(2330-TW)下跌2.11%，鴻海(2317-TW)及聯發科(2454-TW)同步收低，成為壓抑指數的主要力量；台達電(2308-TW)及國巨(2327-TW)則逆勢上漲。類股方面，塑化、泥窯及紡織類股表現較佳，營建及金融類股則相對疲弱，顯示市場資金持續在不同族群間輪動。
法人指出，美股前一交易日全面收高，道瓊工業指數創歷史收盤新高，一度帶動台股盤中反彈，不過台指期夜盤偏弱，加上尾盤獲利了結賣壓，使加權指數終場仍小幅收黑。
南韓股市同樣維持震盪格局。
KOSPI指數終場收盤上漲1.6%，盤中一度上漲2%，也曾下跌約3%，波動幅度仍大。不過市場成交量低於30日平均，顯示進入震盪整理階段。
近期南韓主管機關推出措施限制單一個股槓桿ETF交易，也讓市場投機交易減少。根據資料，KODEX SK海力士單一個股槓桿ETF成交量降至約5,000萬股，遠低於30日平均的2.7億股，顯示去槓桿已近尾聲。
J.P. Morgan指出，以三星電子Samsung Electronics(005930-KR)及SK海力士SK Hynix(000660-KR)為標的的槓桿ETF，資產規模已由6月底約500億美元降至170億美元。該機構認為，南韓市場去槓桿已大致完成，避險基金也已完成約90%的去槓桿作業。
上周五外資更買超南韓股票7.2兆韓元，約50億美元，不僅創下單日新高，也扭轉今年以來持續賣超的態勢。市場普遍認為，近期修正主要來自槓桿資金退場，而非企業基本面轉弱。
美國Balfour Capital Group投資長Steve Lawrence表示，這波修正是「槓桿事件，而非財報事件」。他認為，記憶體產業循環及AI資本支出仍維持成長，三星電子遭到拋售主要是因權重較高，而不是基本面惡化。
美國企業財報也持續支撐市場信心。目前已有近三分之二的標普500企業公布第2季財報，其中84%的企業獲利優於市場預期，且大型科技公司的財報顯示，AI資本支出熱潮仍持續，有助支撐亞洲科技供應鏈。
不過，法國興業銀行分析師指出，AI投資題材正逐漸成熟，投資人開始把焦點放在2026年之後企業能否維持利潤率，而近期南韓科技股獲利預期下修，也成為市場波動的原因之一。
日本股市方面，日經225指數上漲0.2%。
美元兌日圓回升至157.62，部分收復美日上周聯手干預匯市後的跌幅。不過，日圓仍較一周前升值約4%。
此外，日本10年期公債標售需求低於前一次，帶動10年期公債殖利率上升3個基點至2.85%，市場持續關注日本利率及匯率後續變化。
能源市場方面，布蘭特原油上漲1.6%，報每桶85.12美元。市場擔憂荷姆茲海峽航運遇襲可能影響原油供應，使油價自前一交易日低點反彈。
總結來看，美國企業財報持續支撐AI投資題材，但市場已開始關注企業獲利是否能支撐高評價，同時油價、匯率及利率變化也持續牽動亞洲股市表現，台股、韓股與日股短線仍維持震盪整理格局。

paras_en: Asian stock markets were volatile on Tuesday as investors continued to digest U.S. corporate earnings, AI industry outlook, and Middle East tensions. Taiwan's market briefly approached the 44,000‑point round‑number mark during the session, but selling pressure in the final minutes turned it slightly negative; South Korea's market rallied after leveraged‑ETF trading cooled, while Japan's market edged higher, with attention shifting to yen movements and government‑bond yield changes.

Taiwan opened lower but recovered during the session, with the weighted index peaking at 43,912 points, close to 44,000. Selling pressure in the closing minutes pushed the index down 25.75 points to finish at 43,360, a 0.06% decline, on a turnover of NT$1.362 trillion.

Among the blue‑chip stocks, TSMC (2330‑TW) fell 2.11%, while Hon Hai (2317‑TW) and MediaTek (2454‑TW) also closed lower, weighing on the index. Delta Electronics (2308‑TW) and Yageo (2327‑TW) rose against the trend. Sector‑wise, plastics, cement and textiles performed relatively well, whereas construction and financial stocks lagged, indicating continued fund rotation among different groups.

Institutional investors noted that U.S. markets closed broadly higher the previous day, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average hitting a record closing high, which briefly lifted Taiwan's index mid‑session. However, weaker futures after hours and profit‑taking at the close led to a modest net loss for the index.

South Korea's market also remained in a range‑bound pattern. The KOSPI closed up 1.6%, having surged as much as 2% intraday before dipping about 3%, showing still‑large volatility. Trading volume was below the 30‑day average, suggesting a consolidation phase.

Recent measures by Korean regulators to curb single‑stock leveraged‑ETF trading have reduced speculative activity. Data show the KODEX SK Hynix single‑stock leveraged ETF fell to about 50 million shares traded, far below the 30‑day average of 270 million, indicating the de‑leveraging process is nearing completion.

J.P. Morgan reported that leveraged ETFs tracking Samsung Electronics (005930‑KR) and SK Hynix (000660‑KR) shrank from roughly $50 billion at the end of June to $17 billion. The firm believes de‑leveraging in the Korean market is largely finished, with hedge funds having completed about 90% of their de‑leveraging actions.

Foreign investors bought a net 7.2 trillion won (about $5 billion) of Korean stocks on Friday, a single‑day record that reversed a year‑to‑date net‑selling trend. The market generally views the recent correction as driven by the exit of leveraged capital rather than weakening corporate fundamentals.

Steve Lawrence, chief investment officer at Balfour Capital Group, said the correction is a “leveraged event, not an earnings event.” He believes memory‑chip cycles and AI capital spending remain strong, and Samsung’s sell‑off reflects its large weighting rather than deteriorating fundamentals.

U.S. corporate earnings continue to underpin market confidence. Nearly two‑thirds of S&P 500 companies have reported Q2 results, with 84% beating profit expectations, and large‑cap tech earnings show AI‑related capex remains robust, supporting the Asian tech supply chain.

However, analysts at Societe Generale warned that AI investment themes are maturing, and investors are now focusing on whether companies can sustain profit margins beyond 2026. Recent downward revisions to earnings forecasts for Korean tech stocks also contributed to market volatility.

In Japan, the Nikkei 225 rose 0.2%. The dollar regained ground against the yen, reaching ¥157.62, partially recouping losses after coordinated intervention last week, though the yen remains about 4% stronger than a week earlier.

Japanese 10‑year government bond demand was weaker than the previous auction, pushing the 10‑year yield up three basis points to 2.85%. Markets continue to watch developments in Japanese rates and the yen.
On the energy front, Brent crude rose 1.6% to $85.12 a barrel as concerns grew that attacks in the Hormuz Strait could disrupt oil supplies, prompting a rebound from the previous day’s low.

In summary, U.S. earnings continue to support AI‑related investment themes, but markets are now scrutinizing whether corporate profits can justify lofty valuations. At the same time, oil prices, currency moves and interest‑rate shifts keep influencing Asian equity performance, leaving Taiwan, Korea and Japan in short‑term consolidation.

items.title: 金價攻勢熄火？聯準會升息警報再響 短線恐面臨轉折
items.title_en: Gold Price Rally Loses Steam? Fed Rate Hike Warning Sounds Again, Short-Term Reversal Feared
paras: 2026年08月04日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 國際金價周二小幅走高，市場一方面關注美國與伊朗關係發展帶來的避險需求，另一方面等待本周一連串美國就業數據，以判斷聯準會是否可能在9月恢復升息。雖然地緣政治風險支撐金價，但升息預期仍限制黃金上行空間，市場普遍認為金價目前仍處於高檔整理階段。
截稿前，現貨黃金上漲0.2%至每盎司4,061.96美元；美國黃金期貨上漲0.7%至每盎司4,118.30美元。
本周市場焦點將集中在美國勞動市場數據，包括周二公布的職缺數據（JOLTS）、周三的ADP民間就業報告，以及周五最受關注的非農就業報告。這些數據將影響市場對聯準會利率政策的預期。
孟買Kedia Commodities董事Ajay Kedia表示，目前金價正處於整理階段，若就業市場出現降溫跡象，將可能削弱美元，進一步帶動金價走高。
不過，從近期市場邏輯來看，影響金價的關鍵仍是聯準會升息預期，而升息預期又與能源價格及通膨息息相關。
近期中東局勢推升油價，市場擔心能源成本上升將再度推高通膨。如果油價持續高檔，企業的運輸、製造及物流成本都將增加，最終可能反映到商品價格，進一步提高整體通膨壓力。
當通膨升高時，聯準會通常會透過升息抑制物價，因此市場開始提高對9月升息的預期。目前利率期貨顯示，交易員預估聯準會9月升息的機率約為65%。
然而，這類由能源價格上漲帶動的通膨，與經濟需求強勁造成的通膨有所不同。若經濟成長已開始放緩，升息雖有助於抑制物價，卻也可能進一步壓抑經濟活動，因此市場對每一項經濟數據都格外敏感。
黃金雖然一向被視為對抗通膨的避險工具，但由於本身不會產生利息收益，因此當利率提高時，相較於可提供固定收益的存款或債券，吸引力便會下降。
花旗在最新報告中指出，預估金價未來一個月可能持續整理甚至回落，但隨後可望重新走升，預估今年第四季可望升至每盎司4,500美元，並於2027年上半年挑戰5,000美元。
